# Learning objectives

In this lab, we will treat stream gages as windows into **integrated watershed behavior**.

# Clone the GitHub repository

Our course repository is:

<https://github.com/kellyloria/GPHS_782_watershed_sci_seminar.git>

# Explore USGS Water Data

Before writing code, open:

- USGS Water Data for the Nation: <https://waterdata.usgs.gov/>
- `dataRetrieval` documentation: <https://water.code-pages.usgs.gov/dataRetrieval/>

The `dataRetrieval` package provides R functions that construct requests to the modern USGS Water Data APIs.

For this class, we will use functions beginning with:

``` text
read_waterdata_*
```

# Install and load packages

Run these installation lines once if needed.

```{r packages, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c(
  "dataRetrieval",
  "tidyverse",
  "lubridate",
  "scales"
))
```

Load packages:

```{r libraries}
library(dataRetrieval)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)

# stats packages: 
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)

```

# Our watersheds

We will compare two Lake Tahoe tributaries with the much larger Truckee River.

```{r sites}
sites <- tribble(
  ~site_name,        ~monitoring_location_id, ~drainage_area_mi2,
  "Blackwood Creek", "USGS-10336660",          11.2,
  "Incline Creek",   "USGS-10336700",           6.74,
  "Truckee River",   "USGS-10348000",        1067
)

sites
```

The sites differ greatly in drainage area, so **total discharge volume** and **watershed-normalized runoff** answer different questions.

# Look up station metadata with the API

```{r site-metadata}
site_metadata <- read_waterdata_monitoring_location(
  monitoring_location_id = sites$monitoring_location_id
)

site_metadata %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(
    any_of(c(
      "id",
      "monitoring_location_id",
      "monitoring_location_name",
      "state_name",
      "county_name",
      "hydrologic_unit_code",
      "drainage_area"
    ))
  )
```

# USGS parameter codes

For the live code remove temperature

```{r parameter-codes}
parameter_codes <- tribble(
  ~parameter_code, ~variable,
  "00060", "Discharge",
  "63680", "Turbidity"
)

parameter_codes
```

Ask what the parameter codes mean:

```{r parameter-metadata}
parameter_metadata <- read_waterdata_parameter_codes(
  parameter_code = parameter_codes$parameter_code
)

parameter_metadata %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(any_of(c(
    "parameter_code",
    "parameter_name",
    "parameter_description",
    "unit_of_measure"
  )))
```

# Check data availability before downloading

A common mistake is assuming that every USGS gage measures every variable.

```{r time-series-meta}
ts_metadata <- read_waterdata_ts_meta(
  monitoring_location_id = sites$monitoring_location_id
) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  left_join(
    sites %>%
      select(
        monitoring_location_id,
        drainage_area_mi2
      ),
    by = "monitoring_location_id"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
    drainage_area_km2 = drainage_area_mi2 * 2.58999
  )

names(ts_metadata)
```

Filter for the variables we care about:

```{r availability}
availability <- ts_metadata %>%
  filter(
    parameter_code == "00060",
    computation_period_identifier == "Daily"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    parameter_codes %>%
      filter(parameter_code == "00060"),
    by = "parameter_code"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    sites,
    by = "monitoring_location_id"
  ) %>%
  select(
    any_of(c(
      "site_name",
      "monitoring_location_id",
      "drainage_area_mi2",
      "drainage_area_km2",
      "variable",
      "parameter_code",
      "computation_period_identifier",
      "begin",
      "end",
      "begin_date",
      "end_date",
      "unit_of_measure"
    ))
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_name)

availability
```

Because metadata fields can evolve, `any_of()` keeps the display step from failing if a column name changes.

# Define a water year

We will compare multiple years

Let's pick 2022- 2024

Type in: 2021-10-01

```{r dates}

start_date <- as.Date("2022-10-01") # 
end_date   <- as.Date("2024-09-30")

start_date
end_date
```

Water Year 2024 begins October 1, 2023 and ends September 30, 2024.

# Download daily mean discharge

For discharge, we do not need every 15-minute observation.

- Parameter `00060` = discharge
- Statistic `00003` = mean daily

```{r download-discharge}
q_daily <- read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = sites$monitoring_location_id,
  parameter_code = "00060",
  statistic_id = "00003",
  time = c(start_date, end_date)
) %>%
  as_tibble()

glimpse(q_daily)
```

Clean the discharge data:

```{r clean-discharge}

q_daily_clean <- q_daily %>%
  transmute(
    monitoring_location_id,
    date = as.Date(time),
    discharge_cfs = as.numeric(value),
    discharge_cms = discharge_cfs * 0.0283168
  ) %>%
  # Join selected site and metadata information
  left_join(
    availability %>%
      select(
        site_name,
        monitoring_location_id,
        drainage_area_km2,
        variable
      ),
    by = "monitoring_location_id"
  ) %>%
  # Normalize discharge by drainage area
  mutate(
    discharge_cms_km2 = discharge_cms / drainage_area_km2
  )

head(q_daily_clean)
```

# Check discharge completeness

```{r q-completeness}
q_completeness <- q_daily_clean %>%
  group_by(site_name) %>%
  summarise(
    first_date = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_date = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    days_with_data = n_distinct(date[!is.na(discharge_cfs)]),
    missing_q_values = sum(is.na(discharge_cfs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

q_completeness
```

# Plot the hydrographs

discharge_cfs

```{r hydrographs, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(q_daily_clean, aes(x = date, y = discharge_cfs, color=site_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ site_name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Daily mean discharge (ft"^3*"/s)")
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Plot the catchment normalized flow

discharge_cms_km2

```{r hydrographs, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(q_daily_clean, aes(x = date, y = discharge_cms_km2, color=site_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Daily mean discharge (" * m^3 ~ s^-1 ~ km^-2 * ")")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Download high-frequency turbidity

Use the continuous-values API for sensor observations.

Enter the the parameter code for turbidity: 63680

```{r download-continuous}
sensor_data <- read_waterdata_continuous(
  monitoring_location_id = sites$monitoring_location_id,
  parameter_code = c("63680"),
  time = c(start_date, end_date)
) %>%
  as_tibble()

glimpse(sensor_data)
```

This request may take longer because continuous records contain many observations.

# Clean the sensor data

```{r clean-sensors}
sensor_clean <- sensor_data %>%
  transmute(
    monitoring_location_id,
    datetime = as.POSIXct(time),
    parameter_code,
    value = as.numeric(value),
    unit_of_measure = unit_of_measure
  ) %>%
  left_join(parameter_codes, by = "parameter_code") %>%
  left_join(sites, by = "monitoring_location_id")

sensor_clean %>%
  count(site_name, variable)
```

# Summarize turbidity carefully

Turbidity parameter `63680` is reported in FNU.

First calculate daily summaries.

```{r daily-turbidity}
turbidity_daily <- sensor_clean %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(site_name, date) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_turbidity_fnu = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_turbidity_fnu = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_turbidity_fnu = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

turbidity_daily
```

# Compare mean turbidity among watersheds

```{r turbidity-summary}
turbidity_summary <- turbidity_daily %>%
  group_by(site_name) %>%
  summarise(
    days_with_data = n(),
    mean_daily_turbidity_fnu = mean(mean_turbidity_fnu, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_daily_turbidity_fnu = median(mean_turbidity_fnu, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_daily_turbidity_fnu = max(max_turbidity_fnu, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

turbidity_summary
```

Turbidity does not scale directly with watershed area.

```{r turbidity-barplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
ggplot(
  turbidity_summary,
  aes(
    x = reorder(site_name, mean_daily_turbidity_fnu),
    y = mean_daily_turbidity_fnu, fill= site_name
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean daily turbidity (FNU)",
    title = "Mean turbidity during Water Year 2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Turbidity through time

mean_turbidity_fnu

```{r turbidity-time, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(turbidity_daily, aes(x = date, y = mean_turbidity_fnu, color=site_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  #facet_wrap(~ site_name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Daily mean turbidity (FNU)",
    title = "Turbidity is episodic"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Put discharge and turbidity together

```{r join-q-turbidity}
q_turbidity <- q_daily_clean %>%
  select(site_name, date, discharge_cfs, discharge_cms_km2) %>%
  inner_join(
    turbidity_daily %>%
      select(site_name, date, mean_turbidity_fnu),
    by = c("site_name", "date")
  )

head(q_turbidity)
```

# Plot turbidity against catchment normalized stream flow:

discharge_cms_km2

```{r q-turbidity-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(
  q_turbidity,
  aes(x = discharge_cms_km2, y = mean_turbidity_fnu, color=site_name)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_name, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = expression("Daily mean discharge (" * m^3 ~ s^-1 ~ km^-2 * ")"),
    y = "Daily mean turbidity (FNU; log scale)",
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Try adding: #scale_x_log10() + #scale_y_log10() +

# Relationship between turbidity and catchment normalized stream flow?

mean_turbidity_fnu \~ discharge_cms_km2,

```{r flow-turbidity}

# model 
site_models <- q_turbidity %>%
  group_by(site_name) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(
      data,
      ~ glm( mean_turbidity_fnu ~ discharge_cms_km2,
        data = .x,
        family = gaussian()
      )
    )
  )

site_model_results <- site_models %>%
  mutate(
    results = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  select(site_name, results) %>%
  unnest(results)

site_model_results

```

### What those flow slopes mean for this generalized linear model:

| Site            | Flow slope | Interpretation              |
|-----------------|-----------:|-----------------------------|
| Blackwood Creek |       35.8 | +1 m³ s⁻¹ km⁻² = +35.8 FNU  |
| Incline Creek   |      195.4 | +1 m³ s⁻¹ km⁻² = +195.4 FNU |
| Truckee River   |      666.9 | +1 m³ s⁻¹ km⁻² = +666.9 FNU |

# Functional flow calcs:

```{r flow-events}
q_flow <- q_daily_clean %>%
  arrange(site_name, date) %>%
 # organize by water year
   mutate(
    water_year = if_else(
      month(date) >= 10,
      year(date) + 1L,
      year(date)
    ),
    # organize by day of water year
    wy_day = as.integer(
      date - as.Date(paste0(water_year - 1, "-09-30"))
    )
  )
```

Peak flow here as 90 percentile flows for each stream (q90)

Low flows as the 10 percentile flows for each stream (q25)

```{r flow-events-peak}

flow_thresholds <- q_flow %>%
  group_by(site_name, water_year) %>%
  summarise(
    q90 = quantile(
      discharge_cms_km2,
      0.90,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    q25 = quantile(
      discharge_cms_km2,
      0.25,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# High-flow observations
q_peakflow <- q_turbidity %>%
  left_join(
    flow_thresholds,
    by = "site_name"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    discharge_cms_km2 >= q90
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    flow_type = "peak"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_name, date)


# Low-flow observations
q_lowflow <- q_turbidity %>%
  left_join(
    flow_thresholds,
    by = "site_name"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    discharge_cms_km2 <= q25
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    flow_type = "low"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site_name, date)


# Combine
f_flow_dat <- bind_rows(
  q_peakflow,
  q_lowflow
)
```

How much does turbidity correlate with peak flows?

```{r turbidity-time, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(f_flow_dat, aes(x=discharge_cms_km2, y = mean_turbidity_fnu, color=flow_type)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ site_name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Daily mean turbidity (FNU)",
    title = "Peakflow (Q90) and turbidity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r function-flow-turbidity}

site_models <- f_flow_dat %>%
  group_by(site_name) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(
      data,
      ~ glm(
        mean_turbidity_fnu ~ flow_type,
        data = .x,
        family = gaussian()
      )
    )
  )


site_model_results <- site_models %>%
  mutate(
    results = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  select(site_name, results) %>%
  unnest(results)

site_model_results

```

| Site | Low-flow turbidity (FNU) | Increase during peak flow (FNU) | Peak-flow turbidity (FNU) |
|------------------|-----------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|
| Blackwood Creek | 0.57 | **+6.47** | 7.04 |
| Incline Creek | 3.94 | **+6.51** | 10.45 |
| Truckee River | 5.58 | **+8.21** | 13.79 |
